title: Robot teachers
passage:
If you think of the jobs robots could never do, you would probably put doctors and teachers at the top of the list. It's easy to imagine robot cleaners and factory workers, but some jobs need human connection and creativity. But are we underestimating what robots can do? In some cases, they already perform better than doctors at diagnosing illness. Also, some patients might feel more comfortable sharing personal information with a machine than a person. Could there be a place for robots in education after all?

British education expert Anthony Seldon thinks so. And he even has a date for the robot takeover of the classroom: 2027. He predicts robots will do the main job of transferring information and teachers will be like assistants. Intelligent robots will read students' faces, movements and maybe even brain signals. Then they will adapt the information to each student. It's not a popular opinion and it's not possible robots will ever have empathy and the ability to really connect with humans like another human can.

One thing is certain, though. A robot teacher is better than no teacher at all. In some parts of the world, there aren't enough teachers and 9–16 per cent of children under the age of 14 don't go to school. That problem could be partly solved by robots because they can teach anywhere and won't get stressed, or tired, or move somewhere for an easier, higher-paid job.

Those negative aspects of teaching are something everyone agrees on. Teachers all over the world are leaving because it is a difficult job and they feel overworked. Perhaps the question is not 'Will robots replace teachers?' but 'How can robots help teachers?' Office workers can use software to do things like organize and answer emails, arrange meetings and update calendars. Teachers waste a lot of time doing non-teaching work, including more than 11 hours a week marking homework. If robots could cut the time teachers spend marking homework and writing reports, teachers would have more time and energy for the parts of the job humans do best.
passage_uz:
Agar siz robotlar hech qachon bajara olmaydigan kasblar haqida o‘ylasangiz, ehtimol ro‘yxatning eng yuqori qismiga shifokorlar va o‘qituvchilarni qo‘yasiz. Robot farroshlar va zavod ishchilarini tasavvur qilish oson, ammo ba’zi kasblar insoniy aloqa va ijodkorlikni talab qiladi. Lekin biz robotlar nima qila olishini yetarlicha baholamayapmizmi? Ayrim holatlarda ular allaqachon kasalliklarga tashxis qo‘yishda shifokorlardan ko‘ra yaxshiroq natija ko‘rsatmoqda. Shuningdek, ba’zi bemorlar shaxsiy ma’lumotlarni insondan ko‘ra mashina bilan bo‘lishishni qulayroq deb bilishlari mumkin. Oxir-oqibat ta’limda robotlar uchun joy topilishi mumkinmi?

Britaniyalik ta’lim bo‘yicha ekspert Entoni Seldon shunday deb hisoblaydi. Va u hatto sinf xonasini robotlar egallashi uchun aniq yilni ham belgilagan: 2027-yil. Uning bashoratiga ko‘ra, ma’lumotlarni uzatishdek asosiy vazifani robotlar bajaradi, o‘qituvchilar esa yordamchi bo‘lib qoladi. Aqlli robotlar o‘quvchilarning yuz ifodalarini, harakatlarini va hatto miya signallarini o‘qiy oladi. So‘ngra ular ma’lumotlarni har bir o‘quvchiga moslashtiradi. Bu ommabop fikr emas va robotlar hech qachon boshqa inson kabi empatiyaga va insonlar bilan chinakam bog‘lanish qobiliyatiga ega bo‘lishi mumkin emas.

Biroq bir narsa aniq: robot o‘qituvchi umuman o‘qituvchisiz qolishdan yaxshiroqdir. Dunyoning ba’zi joylarida o‘qituvchilar yetishmaydi va 14 yoshgacha bo‘lgan bolalarning 9–16 foizi maktabga bormaydi. Bu muammoni qisman robotlar hal qilishi mumkin, chunki ular istalgan joyda dars bera oladi va stressga tushmaydi, charchamaydi yoki osonroq, maoshi yuqori ish qidirib boshqa joyga ketmaydi.

O‘qituvchilikning bu salbiy jihatlariga hamma qo‘shiladi. Butun dunyoda o‘qituvchilar bu qiyin kasb bo‘lgani va o‘zlarini haddan tashqari ko‘p ishlagandek his qilganliklari uchun ishdan ketishmoqda. Ehtimol, savol 'Robotlar o‘qituvchilarning o‘rnini egallaydimi?' emas, balki 'Robotlar o‘qituvchilarga qanday yordam bera oladi?' bo‘lishi kerakdir. Ofis xodimlari elektron xatlarni tartibga solish va javob berish, uchrashuvlar tashkil qilish va taqvimlarni yangilash kabi ishlarni bajarish uchun dasturiy ta’minotdan foydalanishlari mumkin. O‘qituvchilar dars berishdan tashqari ishlarga ko‘p vaqt sarflaydilar, jumladan, haftasiga 11 soatdan ko‘proq vaqtni uy vazifalarini tekshirishga sarflashadi. Agar robotlar o‘qituvchilarning uy vazifalarini tekshirish va hisobotlar yozishga sarflaydigan vaqtini qisqartira olsa, o‘qituvchilarda insonlar eng yaxshi bajaradigan vazifalar uchun ko‘proq vaqt va quvvat qolgan bo‘lardi.

title: Exams & Education (Noah, Olivia & Ava)
title_uz: Imtihonlar va Ta’lim (Noah, Olivia va Ava)
audio_transcript:
Noah (1): I used to dread exams throughout my student life. To be honest, I still have occasional nightmares about my university finals because the entire experience was so intensely stressful. But now that I am working, I realize that a good worker isn't necessarily someone who scored straight A's in exams, but someone who is creative, adaptable, and takes genuine responsibility for their work.

Olivia (2): When I was at school, I was always the top student. My classmates' parents would constantly tell their children, 'Why can't you be more like Olivia?' because my high exam grades and academic discipline made me very popular with our teachers. However, once I entered the corporate office, I noticed that my colleagues who had average exam scores are performing exceptionally well, leading teams, and getting promoted faster. It sometimes makes me feel content with their success, yet surprised at how real-world demands differ from school tests.

Ava (3): I firmly believe that exams are essential and should not be dismissed. Critics often say that exams only test memorization and recall ability, but a well-designed exam tests all sorts of skills besides simple memorizing — including structured thought processes, analytical ability, problem-solving, and logic. However, I agree that multiple-choice exams alone are not always a good way to test a person's complete, practical abilities.
audio_transcript_uz:
Noah (1): Men talabalik davrimda imtihonlardan doim qo‘rqardim. Rostini aytsam, universitetdagi bitiruv imtihonlari juda kuchli stress bo‘lgani sababli hozir ham vaqti-vaqti bilan tushimga kirib chiqadi. Ammo hozir ishlayotganimda tushundimki, yaxshi xodim — bu faqat a’lo baholarga ega bo‘lgan emas, balki ijodkor, moslashuvchan va o‘z ishiga haqiqiy mas’uliyat bilan qaraydigan insondir.

Olivia (2): Maktabda o‘qiganimda men doim eng namunali o‘quvchi bo‘lganman. Sinfdoshlarimning ota-onalari doimo o‘z farzandlariga: 'Nega Oliviyaga o‘xshamaysan?' deyishardi, chunki mening yuqori baholarim meni o‘qituvchilar orasida juda mashhur qilgan edi. Biroq ofisda ish boshlaganimda, o‘rtacha baholarga o‘qigan hamkasblarim ajoyib natijalar ko‘rsatayotganini, jamoalarni boshqarayotganini ko‘rdim.

Ava (3): Men imtihonlar juda zarur va ularni inkor etib bo‘lmaydi deb hisoblayman. Tanqidchilar ko‘pincha imtihonlar faqat yod olish qobiliyatini tekshiradi deyishadi, ammo puxta tuzilgan imtihon shunchaki eslab qolishdan tashqari, analitik qobiliyat, mantiqiy fikrlash kabi barcha ko‘nikmalarni sinovdan o‘tkazadi. Shunday bo‘lsa-da, faqat ko‘p variantli (multiple-choice) testlarning o‘zi insonning amaliy qobiliyatlarini to‘liq baholash uchun har doim ham eng yaxshi yo‘l emas.
